% Preamble for the generated CV documents.
%
% This file is inlined verbatim into every file in latex/generated/ so that each
% .tex is self-contained: it can be handed to a collaborator, uploaded to
% Overleaf, or compiled anywhere with a TeX Live installation and no other
% files from this repository.
%
% Compile with xelatex (twice, so the page-count reference resolves).
%
% The layout mirrors the web CV (src/components/cv/): ragged-right text, muted
% list markers, ink-colored heading links, generous space between entries and
% sections, and an aligned label column in the skills section.

% article accepts 10, 11 or 12pt only. Anything else is silently ignored.
\documentclass[10pt,letterpaper]{article}

\usepackage[
  letterpaper,
  top=0.72in,
  bottom=0.82in,
  left=0.88in,
  right=0.88in,
  footskip=0.42in

% TeX Gyre ships with every TeX Live installation, so these never fall back to
% a substitute. Pagella is a Palatino clone; Heros is a Helvetica clone.
%
% Loaded by filename rather than by family name: kpathsea finds these in the
% texmf tree on any TeX Live, whereas the family-name form additionally
% requires the fonts to be registered with the operating system.
\setmainfont{texgyrepagella}[
  Extension = .otf,
  UprightFont = *-regular,
  BoldFont = *-bold,
  ItalicFont = *-italic,
  BoldItalicFont = *-bolditalic
]
\newfontfamily\cvsansfont{texgyreheros}[
  Extension = .otf,
  UprightFont = *-regular,
  BoldFont = *-bold,
  ItalicFont = *-italic,
  BoldItalicFont = *-bolditalic
]

\definecolor{cvink}{HTML}{16181D}
\definecolor{cvaccent}{HTML}{1F3A5F}
\definecolor{cvmuted}{HTML}{5A6472}
\definecolor{cvrule}{HTML}{B9BFC9}

\color{cvink}

\hypersetup{
  colorlinks=true,
  urlcolor=cvaccent,
  linkcolor=cvaccent,
  breaklinks=true,
  pdfborder={0 0 0}
}

% --- Vertical rhythm --------------------------------------------------------

% Pagella sets dense at single spacing; a little extra leading opens the page.
\linespread{1.07}

% Ragged right, matching the web layout. Justifying 10pt text across a full
% letter page produces uneven word spacing that reads as noise. \RaggedRight
% (ragged2e) still hyphenates, so the rag stays tidy.
\AtBeginDocument{\RaggedRight}

% Never strand the first or last line of a paragraph across a page break.
\clubpenalty=10000
\widowpenalty=10000

% Hyphenation discipline. Capitalized words are never broken (this CV is dense
% with acronyms and product names — "AC-CESS" is not a good look), two-letter
% stubs like "au-" are forbidden, and consecutive hyphenated line ends or a
% hyphen into a paragraph's short last line are heavily penalized. Ragged
% right gives TeX enough slack that these cost nothing.
\uchyph=0
\lefthyphenmin=3
\doublehyphendemerits=100000
\finalhyphendemerits=400000

\emergencystretch=1.5em
\setlength{\parindent}{0pt}
\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}

% Space between two entries. Roughly half a line: enough that heading/organi-
% zation pairs read as one unit, clearly separate from their neighbors. The
% first entry after a section heading suppresses it (the toggle is set by the
% section title's after-code below), so the heading's own after-space is not
% doubled and entry sections open as tightly as list sections.
\newcommand{\cventrysep}{\vspace{7pt plus 2pt minus 1pt}}
\newtoggle{cvaftersec}

% --- Section headings -------------------------------------------------------

\titleformat{\section}
  {\cvsansfont\normalsize\bfseries\scshape\color{cvaccent}}

\titlespacing*{\section}{0pt}{3.3ex plus .6ex minus .3ex}{1.7ex}

% --- Document furniture -----------------------------------------------------

\newlength{\cvbodywidth}

% \cvheader{name}{credentials}{headline}{contact line}
\newcommand{\cvheader}[4]{%
  \begin{center}
    {\cvsansfont\LARGE\bfseries\color{cvink}#1}%
    \ifstrempty{#2}{}{\\[0.45em]{\cvsansfont\normalsize\color{cvmuted}#2}}%
    \ifstrempty{#3}{}{\\[0.55em]{\small\itshape\color{cvaccent}#3}}%
    \ifstrempty{#4}{}{\\[0.6em]{\cvsansfont\footnotesize #4}}%
  \end{center}
  \vspace{0.2em}%
}

% \cventry{dates}{heading}{subheading}{location}
% Two top-aligned boxes keep the dates flush right even when the heading wraps.
%
% Heading and subheading links are recolored to match their surrounding text —
% ink and muted respectively — as on the web, where entry titles are links
% without being loud about it. Navy stays reserved for inline links (contact
% line, DOIs). \hypersetup color changes are local to the minipage group.
% The struts pin the box's first-line height and last-line depth to the strut
% size, so the gap between entries does not vary with ascenders/descenders.
% \RaggedRight (not kernel \raggedright, which minipage resets to) keeps the
% same tidy 2em rag and hyphenation as the surrounding text.
\newcommand{\cventry}[4]{%
  \par\iftoggle{cvaftersec}{\global\togglefalse{cvaftersec}}{\cventrysep}%
  \needspace{2.5\baselineskip}\noindent
  \begin{minipage}[t]{\cvbodywidth}%
    \hypersetup{urlcolor=cvink}%
    \RaggedRight\strut #2\strut%
    \ifstrempty{#3}{}{\\[0.15em]{\hypersetup{urlcolor=cvmuted}\color{cvmuted}#3\strut}}%
  \end{minipage}%
  \hfill
  \begin{minipage}[t]{\cvdatewidth}%
    \raggedleft
    % The leading \strut is taken at the body font size, before the switch to
    % \scriptsize. Without it the smaller text has a shorter ascent, and a [t]
    % minipage aligned on first baselines drops the date below the heading.
    \ifstrempty{#1}{%
      \ifstrempty{#4}{}{{\strut\cvsansfont\scriptsize\itshape\color{cvmuted}#4}}%
    }{%
      {\strut\cvsansfont\scriptsize\color{cvmuted}#1}%
      \ifstrempty{#4}{}{\\[0.15em]{\cvsansfont\scriptsize\itshape\color{cvmuted}#4}}%
    }%
  \end{minipage}%
  \par
}

% \cvnote{text} — a descriptive line under an entry heading, above any bullets.
\newcommand{\cvnote}[1]{\par\vspace{0.4em}{\small #1}\par}

% \cvchips{text} — inline technology labels for a project entry.
\newcommand{\cvchips}[1]{\par\vspace{0.35em}{\cvsansfont\scriptsize\color{cvmuted}#1}\par}

% \cvskill{label}{items}
% An aligned label column, like the web's definition-list layout. The hanging
% indent keeps wrapped item lines aligned with the column edge.
\newlength{\cvskillcolwidth}
\setlength{\cvskillcolwidth}{1.9in}
\newcommand{\cvskill}[2]{%
  \par\vspace{4pt plus 1pt}\noindent
  \hangindent=\cvskillcolwidth\hangafter=1
  \hbox to \cvskillcolwidth{{\bfseries #1}\hfil}#2%
  \par
}

% \cvprose{text} — the profile summary.
\newcommand{\cvprose}[1]{\par#1\par\smallskip}

\section{Profile}
\cvprose{Entrepreneurial clinical AI product builder and technical product leader with 13+ years taking complex products, platforms, and workflows from ambiguous problems to launch. Residency-trained informatics pharmacist who contributed to the electronic prescribing sections of the ONC's 21st Century Cures Act Final Rule, modernized enterprise clinical systems across 80 hospitals and clinics at Mayo Clinic, and served as Staff Clinical Informatics Data Architect at Verily; now a founder, full-stack engineer, and certified nursing assistant who shipped multiple 0-to-1 AI products in the past year, including haau3, a CMS-recognized consumer caregiving platform among the first seven apps in the CMS Medicare App Library. Four years applying AI to product development and evaluation across multilingual conversational AI, retrieval-augmented generation, workflow automation, clinical decision support, and frontier-model benchmarking, with deep roots in health-data standards and interoperability. Equally fluent in clinical and technical domains: translates ambiguous clinical needs into precise specifications, data models, and shipped software, and technical tradeoffs back into terms clinical teams can act on.}

\section{Professional Experience}
\cventry{Jun 2025 – Present}{\textbf{Founder \& AI Product Lead}}{Brian K Fung Media, LLC}{Brandon, FL}
\cvnote{Independent product work, started during a period of full-time family caregiving, which is where haau3 originated.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Conceived and built haau3, a consumer caregiving platform that unifies longitudinal health records and helps patients and caregivers securely access, understand, and share health information; sole builder from concept through general availability, setting the roadmap across identity, interoperability, conversational AI, and caregiver workflows.
  \item Took haau3 to general availability in the CMS Health Tech Ecosystem for both the Conversational AI and Kill the Clipboard use cases, recognized by CMS at the program's first-anniversary event in July 2026; among the first seven apps listed in the CMS Medicare App Library, sourcing records through a TEFCA QHIN and CMS Aligned Network.
  \item Built and iterated Cora, a multilingual text- and voice-based conversational AI assistant grounded in patient-authorized records; combined Gemini Live, RAG, deterministic knowledge retrieval, and source-linked explanations, evolving the UX from text to speech-to-text to speech-to-speech based on caregiver feedback.
  \item Launched Unscripted Rx from 0-to-1 as a pharmacy workforce and recruiting discovery product with 30,000+ connected entities; grew it organically to 10,000+ monthly views with top-10 Google search visibility and built AI-assisted job-posting ingestion and content normalization to reduce manual population and improve coverage.
  \item Built medlistIQ, an auditable medication-reconciliation API that normalizes and deduplicates fragmented medication data; owned product concept, UX, data model, architecture, and implementation end to end.
  \item Advise CEOs, CTOs, CPOs, and product and engineering leaders on AI-enabled product strategy, platform architecture, and EHR-integrated workflows.
\end{itemize}
\cventry{Sep 2024 – Jun 2025}{\textbf{Staff Clinical Informatics Data Architect}}{Verily}{Fairfax, VA}
\cvnote{Promoted to Staff after earning the top company performance rating (5 of 5) in the preceding review cycle; rated significantly above expectations in three of six cycles overall and recognized with a 2024 Verily Values Award.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Directed enterprise FHIR governance as an appointed member of Verily's FHIR Council, defining 200+ implementation guidance artifacts, semantic models, review patterns, and developer tooling, and leading a company-wide proposal for FHIR proficiency assessments.
  \item Designed evaluation frameworks comparing deterministic clinical reasoning with frontier LLM approaches for AI-assisted type 2 diabetes decision support, clarifying accuracy, explainability, safety, and implementation tradeoffs to guide Verily's clinical AI strategy.
  \item Shaped strategic direction for EHR integration through SMART on FHIR, pharmacy management, and externalization of Verily's care platforms, translating digitized care pathways into requirements for productized platform APIs.
  \item Launched Verily's first medical-coding enrichment modules, standardizing procedure (HCPCS) and immunization coding across products, by building a FHIR terminology service that combined BigQuery with a FHIR proxy to an enterprise terminology-management platform, alongside FHIR terminology data-quality measures.
  \item Led harmonization and enrichment of third-party health information exchange data, turning an ambiguous company initiative into a scoped delivery roadmap by mapping C-CDA-to-FHIR transformation complexity and educating cross-functional teams on the tradeoffs.
  \item Advanced a new market opportunity with a value-based care provider by digitizing its clinical care pathways, mapping concepts to FHIR value sets and configuring executable BPM+ models, starting with heart failure and expanding to additional pathways.
  \item Delivered the medical-device shipment backend within Verily's device-integration initiative, extending a unified device data model across first- and third-party devices in support of connected-care programs.
  \item Influenced engineering and product practice through internal publications on EHR integration, Epic data models, device data models, FHIRPath and CQL, and applications of LLMs, establishing shared collaboration channels between informatics and partner teams.
\end{itemize}
\cventry{Apr 2022 – Sep 2024}{\textbf{Senior Clinical Informatics Data Architect}}{Verily}{Fairfax, VA}
\cvnote{Partnered across product, engineering, UX, research, clinical, legal, and privacy teams to translate ambiguous user and clinical needs into implementation-ready architecture, earning 10+ cross-team peer bonuses and mentoring pharmacy informatics interns and early-career engineers.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Drove the Q1 2024 launch of Lightpath for type 1 diabetes with Highmark, earning a director spot bonus and an engineering peer bonus, by resolving launch-critical issues and automating device fulfillment from CRM through FHIR to BigQuery.
  \item Led semantic and workflow architecture using BPM+ and FHIR, producing 100+ CMMN, BPMN, DMN, and data artifacts that connected user journeys and clinical logic to APIs, decisions, and data contracts across all care teams.
  \item Shipped the clinical content behind the Verily Value Suite MVP, a flagship 2022 launch, by modeling 140+ Mayo Clinic heart-failure (HFrEF) pathway concepts into executable decision models and authoring the company's BPM+ modeling style guide.
  \item Established Verily's enterprise terminology-management capability by leading vendor analysis and selection of a clinical terminology and content-management platform, co-leading its implementation, and launching terminology extracts into BigQuery.
  \item Scaled care-pathway authoring beyond the informatics team by enlisting 20+ clinical data managers as authors, fully automating QA/QC of new models with a CI/CD pipeline, and creating FHIR and BPM+ curricula, including 14 tutorial videos among the company's most-viewed internal documentation.
  \item Standardized race and ethnicity data capture across Verily against federal standards and contributed key designs for laboratory results and error handling, care surveys, and professional task workflows adopted by all care teams.
  \item Partnered with data science teams throughout as the clinical and informatics subject-matter expert to build, train, and evaluate machine-learning and deep-learning applications across care programs, shaping training data, clinical validity, and FHIR-aligned model outputs.
  \item Designed Onduo's medication-review pipeline with data science and engineering, authoring the specification mapping model outputs to FHIR and proposing therapeutic-class-to-NDC eligibility mappings using a commercial drug compendium, aligned to ADA 2023 guidelines.
  \item Prototyped executable DMN and BPMN clinical decision models, spanning cardiac assessment, KCCQ-12 scoring, and an end-to-end CMS Enhanced Oncology Model flow, that guided Verily's strategic selection of care-pathway tooling.
  \item Organized and mapped 145 clinical concepts from the Mayo care-pathway program to UMLS, controlled vocabularies, and HL7 FHIR within the first months of joining, reconciling Mayo's existing decision models to eliminate duplicated mapping work.
  \item Served as Verily's pharmacist subject-matter expert for medications, pharmacy, and clinical workflows, consulting across product areas and delivering pharmacy cost-savings analyses, including IV-to-PO conversion opportunities for cardiac surgery populations.
